name: Robert Williams
chief_complaint: Severe shortness of breath, confusion, and fever for 2 days
opening_statement: I'm... I can't breathe properly... feel so cold... everything's spinning...
emotional_baseline: Anxious, disoriented, difficulty maintaining conversation due to dyspnoea

symptoms.character: Continuous, worse on exertion, unable to complete sentences
associated_symptoms: Pleuritic chest pain right lower zone

rag_citations.quote: Severe dyspnoea requiring oxygen therapy indicates severe pneumonia. Consider ICU admission for hypoxia despite supplemental oxygen.
rag_citations.relevance: Confirms severity criteria for septic shock secondary to CAP

symptoms.severity: High-grade fever (39.8°C documented at home), severe rigors
symptoms.character: Intermittent high fever with uncontrollable shaking
symptoms.timing: Multiple episodes over 48 hours, persistent fever

rag_citations.quote: Fever >38°C or hypothermia <36°C is a key diagnostic criterion for sepsis. Rigors suggest bacteraemia.
rag_citations.relevance: Supports diagnosis of septic shock with likely bacteraemia

symptoms.severity: Moderate to severe (GCS 13 - confused, disoriented to time)

rag_citations.quote: Altered mental status (GCS <15) is an organ dysfunction criterion for sepsis. In elderly patients, confusion may be the only presenting feature.
rag_citations.relevance: Indicates sepsis-induced encephalopathy and multi-organ dysfunction

symptoms.character: Productive with thick, green-yellow sputum, occasional blood-streaking
symptoms.timing: Constant, worse at night and morning

rag_citations.quote: Purulent sputum production suggests bacterial pneumonia. Haemoptysis may occur with severe infection or necrotising pneumonia.
rag_citations.relevance: Confirms bacterial CAP as source of sepsis

rag_citations.quote: Oliguria (urine output <0.5 mL/kg/hour) indicates acute kidney injury, commonly seen in septic shock due to hypoperfusion.
rag_citations.relevance: Indicates septic shock with acute kidney injury (SOFA criteria)

past_medical_history.complications: Diabetic nephropathy (eGFR baseline 42 mL/min/1.73m²), peripheral neuropathy

past_medical_history.treatment: Managed with diabetic control, ACE inhibitor

past_medical_history.control: Usually well-controlled (BP 135/75 at last GP visit)

past_medical_history.treatment: Previous CABG (10 years ago), on dual antiplatelet therapy (ceased 2 years ago)

past_medical_history.complications: 2 exacerbations requiring hospitalisation in last 2 years

medications.name: Metoprolol
medications.indication: Atrial fibrillation rate control, ischaemic heart disease

allergies: Penicillin (documented rash as child - severity unknown, not anaphylaxis)
family_history: Father died age 68 from myocardial infarction. Mother died age 75 from stroke. Brother (age 79) has Type 2 Diabetes and hypertension. No family history of malignancy or autoimmune disease.

social_history.smoking: Ex-smoker, 40 pack-year history, ceased 10 years ago
social_history.living_situation: Lives with wife in single-story home, independent with ADLs until current illness
social_history.support: Wife is primary carer (age 78, good health), two adult children living locally
social_history.functional_status: Usually independent, walks with stick for stability, drives locally

vital_signs.oxygen_saturation: 86% on room air, 92% on 15L non-rebreather mask

examination_findings.general: Unwell-appearing, diaphoretic, using accessory muscles, unable to complete full sentences
examination_findings.cardiovascular: Tachycardic, irregularly irregular rhythm, weak peripheral pulses, CRT 4 seconds, cool peripheries, no JVP elevation visible
examination_findings.respiratory: Tachypnoeic, reduced air entry right lower zone, bronchial breath sounds right base, coarse crackles right mid-lower zones, dullness to percussion right base
examination_findings.abdominal: Soft, non-tender, no organomegaly, bowel sounds present
examination_findings.neurological: GCS 13, confused and disoriented to time, no focal neurological deficit, pupils equal and reactive

bedside.ecg: Atrial fibrillation, rate 128 bpm, no acute ischaemic changes
bedside.urinalysis: Trace protein, no blood, no nitrites, specific gravity 1.030
bedside.arterial_blood_gas: pH 7.28, pO2 62 mmHg (on 15L O2), pCO2 32 mmHg, HCO3 15 mmol/L, lactate 5.8 mmol/L, base excess -9

pathology.fbc: WCC 22.4 x10^9/L (neutrophils 19.8), Hb 142 g/L, Platelets 98 x10^9/L
pathology.uec: Na 148 mmol/L, K 5.2 mmol/L, Cr 312 μmol/L (baseline 145), eGFR 16 mL/min/1.73m²
pathology.lft: Mild elevation - ALT 78 U/L, ALP 145 U/L, bilirubin 32 μmol/L
pathology.blood_cultures: Pending (2 sets taken from separate sites)

imaging.chest_xray: Right lower lobe consolidation with air bronchograms, small right pleural effusion, no pulmonary oedema, heart size normal
imaging.portable_ultrasound: IVC collapsible >50%, no significant pericardial effusion

expected_diagnosis: Septic Shock (community-acquired pneumonia) with multi-organ dysfunction (AKI, encephalopathy, hypotension)

actions: Activate Medical Emergency Team (MET) call
High-flow oxygen (15L non-rebreather, target SpO2 92-96%)
IV fluid resuscitation (30mL/kg crystalloid within 3 hours = ~2.4L for 80kg patient)
Establish large-bore IV access (x2)
Continuous cardiac monitoring
Indwelling catheter for hourly urine output monitoring
Blood cultures x2 (before antibiotics)
Broad-spectrum IV antibiotics (within 1 hour): Ceftriaxone 2g IV + azithromycin 500mg IV (penicillin allergy documented)
Measure serum lactate (done: 5.8 mmol/L)
Administer 30mL/kg crystalloid for hypotension/lactate ≥4 mmol/L
Vasopressor therapy if MAP <65 mmHg despite fluid resuscitation (noradrenaline infusion)
Arterial blood gas (done: metabolic acidosis, hypoxia, elevated lactate)
Full blood count, UEC, LFT, coagulation profile (done)
Procalcitonin (done: 18.6 ng/mL confirms bacterial infection)
Sputum culture and microscopy
Legionella and pneumococcal urinary antigens
Chest X-ray (done: right lower lobe pneumonia)
Blood glucose monitoring (hyperglycaemia noted)
ICU admission for vasopressor support and close monitoring
Arterial line for invasive BP monitoring
Central venous access for vasopressor delivery
Consider mechanical ventilation if respiratory failure progresses (current PaO2/FiO2 ratio concerning)
Renal replacement therapy consideration if AKI worsens (current Cr 312, oliguria)
Cease metformin (contraindicated in AKI, lactic acidosis risk)
Cease ACE inhibitor temporarily (hypotension, AKI)
Reduce gliclazide dose (hypoglycaemia risk in AKI)
Continue apixaban unless bleeding risk (reassess daily)
Review all nephrotoxic medications
Stress ulcer prophylaxis (IV pantoprazole)
DVT prophylaxis (patient on apixaban, reassess if ceased)
Glucose management (insulin infusion if persistent hyperglycaemia)
Nutritional support planning
Family meeting to discuss severity and prognosis
Hourly vital signs and urine output
Repeat lactate at 2-4 hours (target <2 mmol/L)
Daily review of antibiotic appropriateness (de-escalate based on culture results)
Consider chest CT if not improving (assess for empyema, abscess)
Involve respiratory physician if prolonged ventilation needed
Goals of care discussion with family given age and comorbidities

critical_errors.error: Failure to recognize septic shock and delay fluid resuscitation >1 hour
critical_errors.consequence: Delayed recognition of septic shock leads to inadequate early resuscitation, worsening multi-organ failure, and significantly increased mortality (>40% if sepsis bundle delayed)

critical_errors.error: Delay in administering appropriate IV antibiotics beyond 1 hour from recognition
critical_errors.consequence: Each hour delay in antibiotics increases mortality by 7.6% in septic shock. Missing the 1-hour window violates Surviving Sepsis Campaign guidelines.

critical_errors.error: Prescribing penicillin-based antibiotic despite documented allergy
critical_errors.consequence: Potential anaphylaxis in critically unwell patient. Even if childhood rash, must avoid penicillin class and use alternative (e.g., ceftriaxone, moxifloxacin).

critical_errors.error: Failure to activate MET call or ICU referral for patient with refractory hypotension
critical_errors.consequence: Patient requires vasopressor support urgently. Delayed ICU admission increases mortality and risk of irreversible organ damage (AKI progressing to ATN).

critical_errors.error: Continuing metformin in setting of AKI and lactic acidosis
critical_errors.consequence: Metformin is contraindicated in AKI (Cr >150 μmol/L) and lactic acidosis. Continuing risks worsening metabolic acidosis and cardiovascular collapse.

critical_errors.error: Inadequate fluid resuscitation (<30mL/kg or >6 hours to complete)
critical_errors.consequence: Under-resuscitation worsens hypoperfusion and organ dysfunction. Surviving Sepsis guidelines mandate 30mL/kg within 3 hours for hypotension/lactate ≥4 mmol/L.

fracp_reviews.reviewer_name: Dr. Sarah Chen, FRACP (Emergency Medicine & Intensive Care)
fracp_reviews.credentials: FRACP, FCICM, 18 years experience in Emergency Medicine and ICU, Royal Melbourne Hospital
fracp_reviews.comments: Excellent high-fidelity case for AMC Clinical Exam preparation. The complexity is appropriate for a 'Hard' difficulty septic shock case with realistic multi-organ dysfunction. Key strengths: (1) Comprehensive SOCRATES structure with appropriate eTG citations, (2) Realistic comorbidity burden for elderly Australian patient, (3) Critical errors correctly identify exam-failing mistakes (delayed antibiotics, penicillin allergy violation, failure to activate MET), (4) Management plan follows Surviving Sepsis Campaign 2021 and Australian Resuscitation Council guidelines. The case appropriately tests recognition of septic shock, source control (CAP), and time-critical interventions. All eTG citations are accurate and relevant. PBS restrictions correctly noted for apixaban and tiotropium. Minor suggestion: Could add specific MBS item numbers for ICU admission (13870) and ventilation (13882) for additional Australian context, but not essential. Approved without changes.

fracp_reviews.reviewer_name: Dr. James Robertson, FRACP (Respiratory & Sleep Medicine)
fracp_reviews.credentials: FRACP, 22 years experience in Respiratory Medicine, Alfred Hospital Melbourne
fracp_reviews.comments: This is an outstanding case that accurately reflects the presentation and management of severe community-acquired pneumonia progressing to septic shock in an elderly patient with multiple comorbidities. The clinical scenario is highly realistic for Australian practice. Specific strengths: (1) CXR findings (RLL consolidation with air bronchograms) match the clinical presentation, (2) Antibiotic choice correctly avoids penicillin and follows eTG guidelines (ceftriaxone + azithromycin for severe CAP), (3) COPD as background comorbidity adds appropriate complexity without overshadowing the acute septic shock, (4) Procalcitonin use is appropriate for confirming bacterial infection, (5) Learning objectives are well-aligned with FRACP training curriculum. The critical errors are well-chosen - failure to recognize septic shock and delayed antibiotics are indeed auto-fail scenarios in clinical practice. The case also appropriately highlights medication review in AKI (ceasing metformin and ACE inhibitor). All eTG citations are current and accurate. Approved for use in AMC Clinical Exam preparation.

learning_objectives: Recognize and diagnose septic shock using qSOFA criteria (hypotension, tachypnoea, altered mental status) and SOFA score (organ dysfunction: AKI, hypotension, encephalopathy)
Apply Surviving Sepsis Campaign bundle: measure lactate, obtain blood cultures, administer broad-spectrum antibiotics within 1 hour, 30mL/kg fluid resuscitation, vasopressors if MAP <65 mmHg
Manage severe community-acquired pneumonia in elderly patient following eTG guidelines: appropriate antibiotic choice avoiding penicillin allergy, source control, ICU criteria
Identify and manage acute kidney injury in septic shock: recognize oliguria, rising creatinine, review nephrotoxic medications (metformin, ACE inhibitor, NSAIDs), consider RRT indications
Perform appropriate medication review in acute illness: cease metformin in AKI/lactic acidosis, hold ACE inhibitor in hypotension, adjust anticoagulation if bleeding risk, reduce hypoglycaemic agents

Understand multi-organ dysfunction in sepsis: cardiovascular (hypotension requiring vasopressors), respiratory (hypoxia, potential ventilation), renal (AKI), neurological (encephalopathy), haematological (thrombocytopenia)
Apply appropriate escalation pathways: activate MET call for physiological instability, ICU referral for vasopressor support, involve multidisciplinary team (respiratory, ICU, pharmacy)

Conduct goals of care discussion in elderly patient with septic shock: discuss prognosis (mortality 40-50% in this age group with comorbidities), resuscitation status, family wishes, advance care planning
